source_text: Praemissa scilicet disputatione probare contentus te quoque, qui nobis seditionem per hoc maximam concitabas, dicere remissionis peccatorum non in cunctis unam constare rationem, ut etiamsi unum hoc naturale peccatum persuadere possis, tamen liqueret necessario dici non semper accedentium ad gratiam unum statum esse et hoc Apostoli dictum: Ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n172] in adulta solum, non autem etiam in prima aetate compleri.
pass_a_gloss: Namely, content to prove by the disputation sent ahead that you also, who were stirring a very great sedition against us through this, say that the reason of the remission of sins does not stand as one in all, so that even if you could persuade this one natural sin, it would nevertheless be clear that it is necessarily said that there is not always one state of those approaching grace and that this saying of the Apostle: From many offenses into justification is completed only in adult, but not also in the first age.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: In the preceding argument I was content to prove that even you, who stirred up a great uproar against us on this point, say that remission of sins does not follow one identical pattern in everyone. Even if you could persuade us of this one natural sin, it would still be clear that we must say those who approach grace are not always in one condition, and that the apostle’s phrase ‘from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16) is fulfilled only in adulthood, not in earliest infancy as well.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
